voyage.name: Sugar Loaf Mountain
voyage.content: One of the defining landmarks of the city. The cable cars take you up from for a breathtaking view of much of Zona Sul and the center, and also the city of Niteroi, just across Guanabara Bay. You have to queue again at Urca Hill (Morro da Urca) station for the second part of the ride. You can also walk up a trail to this point (start on Trilha do Morro da Urca along the shore, then climb the stairs on your left) and

voyage.name: Christ the Redeemer Statue (Corcovado peak)
voyage.price: R$58 adults, R$32 children/students/seniors (included in price of some transportation)
voyage.content: The 710 m granite peak of Corcovado, capped by the famous 38-m statue of Jesus known as Christ the Redeemer (Cristo Redentor), has been the vantage point for countless picture postcards and travel posters through the ages. Its peak provides a sweeping panorama, from the interior of Guanabara Bay to the north, to Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas (Rodrigo de Freitas' Lagoon) to the south. Access to the mountain as a whole is f

voyage.name: Arpoador
voyage.content: The rocks at the Copacabana end of Ipanema beach. From here you can see a panorama including Corcovado and Sugar Loaf. It is supposed to be the best place to watch the sunset from in Rio. Reputedly a bit dangerous so go there at weekends when there are lots of people and a few police around.

voyage.name: Guanabara Palace
voyage.content: Former palace of the Imperial Princess, now the governor's office. Eclectic architecture. Not open to the public.

voyage.name: Largo do Boticário
voyage.content: A delightful square of well-preserved colonial style houses that date back to 1831.

voyage.name: Laranjeiras Palace
voyage.alt: Palacio das Laranjeiras, literally Palace of the Orange Trees
voyage.content: This is the official residence of the Governor of the State of the Rio de Janeiro

voyage.name: Monumento a Estácio de Sá
voyage.alt: Espaço Cultural do Monumento Estácio de Sá
voyage.content: Erected in 1973. Homage to Estácio de Sá, the founder of Rio de Janeiro

voyage.name: Basilica of the Immaculate Conception on the Botafogo Beach
voyage.alt: Basílica Imaculada Conceição na Praia de Botafogo

voyage.name: Our Lady of the Rosary Parish Church
voyage.alt: Igreja / Paróquia Nossa Senhora do Rosario
voyage.address: 164, R. Gen. Ribeiro da Costa, Leme

voyage.name: Church of Our Lady
voyage.alt: Igreja Matriz de Nossa Senhora da Glória
voyage.address: ~19, Rua Gago Coutinho, Rua das Laranjeiras, s/n°, Largo do Machado

voyage.name: Casa das Canoas
voyage.content: The former residence of architect Oscar Niemeyer. Call in advance.

voyage.name: Museum of Folklore Edison Carrero
voyage.content: Part of the National Centre for Folklore and Popular Culture (CNFCP). The museum was created in 1968 and today has around 13,000 objects by various authors, techniques and origins, kept in technical archives, available for consultation by institution-related post-graduate specialists, by appointment.

voyage.name: Indian Museum
voyage.content: Focusing on the history of Native Brazilians, with many artifacts including a home of the Umé culture. The gift shop has authentic handicrafts.

voyage.name: Carmen Miranda Museum
voyage.content: Here you'll find an amusing collection of photographs, posters, musical recordings, and, of course, gigantic fruity hats worn by the singing star. The building looks like an abandoned space capsule in the middle of the park.

voyage.name: Army History Museum of Copacabana Fort
voyage.alt: Museu Histórico do Exército e Forte de Copacabana
voyage.price: Adults R$6, over 60 years old R$3, students with student ID R$3
voyage.hours: Exhibition Halls: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00. Observatories, Souvenir Vitacura, Colombo Confectionery and 18 do Forte Coffee Shop: Tue-Sun 10:00-20:00
voyage.address: Praça Coronel Eugênio Franco, 1 - Posto 6 - Copacabana

voyage.name: Museum of the Republic
voyage.content: The former presidential palace (1893-1960) hosts a museum of recent history and nice gardens, with an adjacent art gallery and small theatre that occasionally shows free movies. One of main features is the room where president Getúlio Vargas shot himself in 1954.

voyage.name: Museu Villa-Lobos
voyage.content: Heitor Villa-Lobos wrote about 1000 pieces and is considered one of the world's greatest composers. This small collection includes a number of personal items, musical instruments, pictures and hand-written work by Villa-Lobos.

voyage.name: Oi Futuro
voyage.content: This former telephone museum hosts a fine gallery with temporary exhibitions of digital art or art with interactive medias; it is sponsored by the local phone company.

voyage.name: Instituto Moreira Salles (IMS)
voyage.address: Rua Marques de São Vicente 476, Gavea
voyage.content: Cultural Centre - at these days hosting a photo exhibition of the construction of Brasilia. Guided tours: Tu-F at 17:00.

voyage.name: Botanical Garden
voyage.content: Planted in the 1800s, it is both a park and a scientific laboratory. It contains a huge collection of plants from all over the world, not only tropical ones. If you take the bus note that Jardim Botanico is also the name of a neighborhood and the road on which it is found so make sure you go all the way to the entrance. The gardens are well kept and very lush. Not far from the cafe, you are likely to hear swooshing s

voyage.name: Parque Enrique Lage
voyage.content: Public park with walking trails through subtropical forest. A cafe offers drinks and meals. A trail goes up to Corcovado mountain from here. The land was the residence of industrialist Enrique Lage and his wife, singer Gabriella Besanzoni. During the 1920s Lage had the mansion remodeled by Italian architect Mario Vodrel, with interior paintings by Salvador Payols Sabaté. The mansion was notably featured in the 2003 m

voyage.name: Flamengo Park
voyage.address: along the bay between Flamengo and Glória
voyage.content: 1.2 million m² with broad walkways, Flamengo Beach, various monuments, and over 10,000 trees. To its north is the Museum of Modern Art (see Centro).

voyage.name: Hike/Climb Sugarloaf Mountain
voyage.alt: Escalada do Costão / Trilha do Pão de Açúcar
voyage.content: If you are keen on hiking and climbing up the full way, check out this trail. Equipment is needed as there is a vertical section with potentially serious consequences in case of a fall. If you do not have your own rock climbing equipment, go with a guide. On the way down you can use the gondola for free to get to Morro da Urca. From there, you can follow an easy trail to get back to the ground.

voyage.name: Cláudio Coutinho Trail
voyage.content: This pleasant walk follows the southern coast of Urca Hill (Morro da Urca), and side trails lead to various points on the hill, offering lush vegetation, monkeys, and nice views of the bay.

voyage.name: Planetarium Espaço Museu do Universo
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00, Sat Sun and public holidays 14:30-17:00
voyage.content: There are shows, mainly for kids, in the planetarium on weekends. These are targeted at different age groups so it is essential to check the age the show you plan to attend is for or you may get stuck with one that is totally unsuitable. From Wednesday to Friday the space is also open without shows and there are around 60 hands-on scientific experiments to entertain kids.

voyage.name: Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon
voyage.content: A large lagoon in the middle of South Zone, with great views to Corcovado and Ipanema and Leblon beaches. You can run, walk, skate or cycle the 7.5 km around this freshwater lake and then retire to your luxurious Ipanema penthouse apartment, or just imagine it! Some have been known to swim in it although pollution levels are very high. Around Lagoa you can rent cycles, swan-shaped pedalos and, on the western side nea

voyage.name: Pedalboats
voyage.address: on Lake Rodrigo de Freitas - Ipanema
voyage.content: Pedal the lake in these swan-shaped boats for 2-5 people.

voyage.name: Quadracycle
voyage.content: Take a ride around the lake on one of these unique contraptions, like a bicycle for two side-by-side riders under a little canopy.

voyage.name: Hanggliding and Paragliding
voyage.content: From the ramp atop Pedra Bonita, qualified instructors offer tandem flight courses in hang gliding, paragliding, and ultralight. Wind conditions are typically safe and offer splendid views of the surrounding beaches and mountains. Helicopter rides also available. Various clubs offer the experience: and [skycenter@skycenter.com.br.

voyage.name: Panoramic helicopter rides
voyage.content: These are noisy and drive Rio's residents mad as the helicopters circle the statue of Christ, but if you can live with that and can afford it, a helicopter trip is likely to be the most memorable experience of your visit to Rio. There are 2 operators in the city:Helisight: You can catch a copter at the first stage of the cable car ride up the Sugar Loaf or, alternatively, on the west edge of Lagoa. The basic trip tak

voyage.name: Helicopter Rider
voyage.address: Av. Gen. Moisés Castelo Branco Filho, 700 - Golf Olímpico - Barra da Tijuca
voyage.content: A helicopter ride over the beautiful beaches and over Sugarloaf Mountain and Christ the Redeemer.

voyage.name: Pedra da Gávea
voyage.content: Hike up this monolith of 844 m and enjoy one of the most spectacular city views in the world. It can be done either by booking a tour or on your own. The round trip takes roughly 4-5 hours and is strenuous and challenging with a stretch of light rock climbing ("Carrasqueira"). Bring enough water and food and wear proper shoes. Attention: There are stories online of people, who got robbed on the hike up.

voyage.name: Hike up the Morro Dois Irmãos
voyage.content: There are two viewpoints in this hike before reaching the final destination of the peak. From the first, you will be able to see Rocinha, which is the largest favela in Latin America, and a clear view of Pedra da Gávea. From the second, you are able to see Serra da Carioca, Gávea, Corcovado (where Christ the Redeemer stands tall), and Pedra Bonita. Once reaching the highest peak of the Morro Dois Irmãos you are able

voyage.name: Urca Beach
voyage.content: Popular with the residents of Urca.

voyage.name: Vermelha Beach
voyage.content: The "red beach". Very safe due to military base, which is nearby.

voyage.name: Leme Beach
voyage.content: Somewhat less crowded than the Copacabana Beach

voyage.name: Copacabana Beach
voyage.content: Among the most famous beaches in the world, Copacabana attracts many tourists, both foreign and national. In summer, there are occasional free evening concerts of big name acts which draw huge crowds.

voyage.name: Ipanema Beach
voyage.content: The main beach for the middle-class, and specifically the Posto 9 section (watchtower #9) is preferred by left-wingers, intellectuals, artists, journalists and similar beach-goers. You can easily walk into a politician or someone famous here. The area close to the Farme de Amoedo street in Ipanema is known to attract the gay crowd of the city, who show off openly their sexuality.

voyage.name: São Conrado Beach
voyage.content: On the other side of the Dois Irmãos mountain west of Leblon, this beach is popular with middle class people and favela dwellers alike. Good surfing and hang-gliding opportunities. Sometimes inappropriate for bathing. The south zone can be seen through a helicopter ride where you can marvel at the magnificent view of the most beautiful beaches in the capital of Rio de Janeiro, as well as flying over monuments

voyage.name: Hippie Fair
voyage.content: Here you will find everything from soapstone Redentor statues to swizzle sticks carved with Amazonian birds. There are several vendors selling the same thing so you can have fun bargaining.

voyage.name: Hype Babalonia
voyage.content: This market has some more upscale merchandise and you will find fewer tourists. It is a place where middle class Cariocas do some bargain shopping.

voyage.name: Pé de Bói
voyage.content: One of the best places to get authentic local handicrafts. A lovely store with many great gift ideas. There are two floors, the first full of items for sale, such as pieces made from wood, ceramic and fibre, fit to decorate any living room space. The second floor is where they sometimes have art exhibits, usually related to Brazilian history, culture or customs from various regions that are distinctly scattered throu

voyage.name: Livraria Argumento
voyage.content: Good selection of English books. Popular with local intellectuals and artists.

voyage.name: Livraria da Travessa
voyage.content: Nice bookshop which allows you to choose a book to peruse while you sip coffee in the café. Small section of foreign-language books.

voyage.name: Botafogo Praia Shopping
voyage.content: Has a food court with a panoramic view.

voyage.name: Casa & Gourmet Shopping
voyage.content: This little mall has good restaurants and shops specialized in things for home from furniture to glasses.

voyage.name: Shopping Leblon
voyage.address: Av. Afrânio de Melo Franco, 290, Leblon
voyage.content: A new and sophisticated mall with 200 stores, 4 cinema screens and a food court that looks out on the Lagoa.

voyage.name: São Conrado Fashion Mall
voyage.content: High-end mall with 140 stores including brand names like Diesel, Fendi, and Emporio Armani.

voyage.name: Shopping Rio Sul
voyage.content: The largest mall in the Zona Sul, with 7 floors and 400 stores.

voyage.name: Shopping da Gávea
voyage.hours: Stores Mon-Sat 10:00-22:00, Sun 13:00-21:00, holidays 14:00-21:00; food and leisure: Mon-Sat 10:00-23:00, Sun and holidays 12:00-23:00
voyage.address: Rua Marquês de São Vicente 52 - Gávea
voyage.content: 200 stores and a movie theater. Services: free Wi-Fi, Family bathrooms; 'Torres' loading ChargeBox, recharge your mobile for free within 30 minutes; carts available for children, motorized wheel chairs; available for withdrawals and payments: Banco do Brasil, Itaú, Caixa e Banco 24 hr; English Support Services for tourist information about the city of Rio de Janeiro; valet parking.

voyage.name: Cervantes
voyage.hours: closes only with the sun raising
voyage.content: The menu is composed by big sandwiches, with whatever you want: ham, salami, cheese, tenderloin and so on, with one home special ingredient: a big pineapple slice. It's a tropical taste to the end of your night. Famous for making their classic filet mignon and pineapple sandwich in the blink of an eye. Look out for the legendary "Penguin Waiter", who've been working there forever. You won't have a problem to find out

voyage.name: Galeria Condor
voyage.content: This two-story shopping arcade has a number of inexpensive Middle Eastern restaurants on the ground floor.

voyage.name: Le Bistrôt Du Cuisinier
voyage.content: Some fine Parisian cuts here, roast duck, whatever you like.

voyage.name: Berbigão
voyage.content: Seafood restaurant with good selection.

voyage.name: Cantina Donanna
voyage.content: Italian cuisine.

voyage.name: Casa da Feijoada
voyage.content: Serves nothing but traditional, authentic Brazilian feijoada.

voyage.name: Filé de Ouro
voyage.content: A good alternative to churrascarias, this steakhouse is simple and cozy. During the weekends there are usually big lines, but the steak is delicious. Try Filé à Oswaldo Aranha, with toasted garlic.

voyage.name: Gula Gula
voyage.content: A trendy restaurant with excellent salads, main dishes and desserts.

voyage.name: Carretão
voyage.content: Good-value rodizio – all-you-can-eat salad and barbecue.

voyage.name: Nam Thai
voyage.content: Fairly authentic and very popular Thai restaurant. Reservations essential at weekends.

voyage.name: New Natural
voyage.content: A good per-kilo restaurant. It is attached to a whole foods shop and has a good buffet selection, including sushi.

voyage.name: Via Sete
voyage.content: This grill restaurant offers a great bang for the buck: from their veranda you get to people-watch pretty Brazilians. There you can enjoy tasty wraps and sandwiches.

voyage.name: Manekineko Leblon
voyage.content: Sushi.

voyage.name: Marius Carnes
voyage.content: One of the best churrascaria in town.

voyage.name: Viva Gastronomia
voyage.address: Av. Nossa Senhora de Copacabana, 796 - Copacabana
voyage.content: Very good all-you-can-eat rodizio.

voyage.name: Zazá Bistrô Tropical
voyage.content: A trendy, sexy and exotic place with great South Asian dishes. Good to go as a couple.

voyage.name: Academia da Cachaça
voyage.content: With over 500 varieties, this is the place to start your studies of Brazil's national drink.

voyage.name: Bip Bip
voyage.content: This unpretentious and thoroughly un-touristy hole-in-the-wall botequim has been a favorite hang-out of top local musicians for decades and hosts regular live choro, samba, and bossanova performances.

voyage.name: Empório
voyage.content: Popular with the younger crowd, that hangs out there to listen to DJs playing rock. Most of the crowd hangs out there because they are underage and can't get in the underground nightclubs. Gets packed with foreigners during summer.

voyage.name: Garota de Ipanema
voyage.address: Rua Vinicius de Moraes and Rua Prudente de Morais - Ipanema
voyage.content: There's no better place in Rio, Brazil, or even the world to watch bathing beauties stroll by than this cafe-bar, named after the song which according to legend was written here in 1962.

voyage.name: Mamma Jamma Pizzeria Rústica
voyage.content: Pizza and draft beer is the name of the game here, though good quality. And save room for dulce de leche.

voyage.name: Casa da Matriz
voyage.content: Nightclub.

voyage.name: Fosfobox
voyage.content: "Fosfo" as it's nicknamed by the goers has a strong Saturday rock-oriented party. Young, trendy crowd with djs playing mostly indie rock, discopunk and electro-rock. After 04:00 it has a more electronic after-party. Different parties happen on Fridays, but it's usually electronic, with favorite genres being electro, house and minimal. Other nights are usually more electronic also, but has had Rock parties also on Thu

voyage.name: Cariocando
voyage.content: A fairly new establishment, offering a bit of Lapa in the Zona Sul. Live music (samba, choro, MPB) Tu-Su. They seem to have a knack for booking the lesser-known offspring and siblings of more famous musicians.

voyage.name: Bar do Tom
voyage.content: Hosts lesser names, mainly performing Brazilian music.

voyage.name: Sala Cecilia Meireles
voyage.content: The city's main venue for classical performances.

voyage.name: Ace Hostel
voyage.content: Basic accommodations in large dormitories. Fabulous breakfast buffet. Excellent value. Right at the beach of Botafogo.

voyage.name: Arpoador Inn
voyage.content: Clean place, older interior, only a sidewalk apart from the beach.

voyage.name: Beija Flor
voyage.content: Typical budget hotel in Catete district. The rooms have no exterior windows and just open into the hallway, so take a look before deciding.

voyage.name: CabanaCopa Hostel
voyage.content: A, unique hostel in the safest part of Copacabana. A large colonial house, fully renovated with spacious ensuite dorms, excellent social areas, great breakfast and friendly, helpful staff.

voyage.name: Che Lagarto Hostel Copacabana
voyage.content: One of the most popular backpackers spots in Copacabana with engrossing New Year's and Carnaval events and a bar next door featuring live music. Big, airy rooms and great common areas, staffed by very knowledgeable, cool young people.

voyage.name: Che Lagarto Hostel Ipanema
voyage.content: Has both private and shared rooms. It is located one block away from the beach. You have access to Wi-Fi, a public kitchen and the bar. The breakfast is included.

voyage.name: Rio Copa Hostel
voyage.content: Free pickup from the airport, breakfast.

voyage.name: Ferreira Viana
voyage.content: As long as you don't mind climbing three flights of stairs (no elevator), this is as good a value as any among the budget hotels in the area, with friendly service.

voyage.name: Jucati
voyage.content: Well equipped apartments with free internet Wi-Fi available.

voyage.name: Riazor
voyage.content: Excellent location and cheap, but the rooms could be nicer.

voyage.name: Terasse Hostel
voyage.price: R$40 in dormitory, R$140 for a couple.

voyage.name: Astoria Copacabana Hotel
voyage.content: Good mid-range hotel. Not to be confused with the more upscale Astoria Palace (below), operated by the same owners.

voyage.name: Rio Design Hotel
voyage.content: This calls itself a Design Hotel. Each floor has a different style of suites that is really what distinguishes this locality. Top floor restaurant for breakfast and a good view of local favelas.

voyage.name: Rio Guesthouse
voyage.content: A boutique guest house on the beachfront, in a 1200-m² penthouse. Beautifully decorated, very comfortable.

voyage.name: Hotel Vermont
voyage.content: Affiliated with the nearby San Marco Hotel and Hotel Carlton in Leblon. Very friendly and helpful service.

voyage.name: Rio INN Art
voyage.content: The Suites has two types of rooms: Private and Private Low Cost. It is 4 blocks away from the beach.

voyage.name: Che Lagarto Suites Copacabana Santa Clara
voyage.content: The Suites has two types of rooms: Private and Private Low Cost. Breakfast, public kitchen and Wi-Fi included.

voyage.name: Astoria Palace Hotel
voyage.content: Fantastic rooftop pool with a great view of the beach.

voyage.name: Belmond Copacabana Palace
voyage.content: An iconic hotel dating to 1923, with a history of hosting the famous and wealthy. Arguably the best hotel in Rio.

voyage.name: Copacabana Praia Hotel
voyage.content: Four-star hotel. Services: pool, restaurant, sauna, Wi-Fi, IDD telephone, safety deposit box, air conditioning, room service, outdoor pool, minibar, laundry, LCD TV, bar.

voyage.name: JW Marriott Hotel Rio de Janeiro
Sheraton Rio Hotel & Resort
voyage.content: The only hotel in the Zona Sul with direct beach access.

voyage.name: Banco do Brasil Cultural Centre
voyage.alt: Centro Cultural do Banco do Brasil - CCBB
voyage.content: A cultural centre with gallery, movie theatre, video room, library and stages; usually hosts the main exhibitions in town. An interesting building completed in 1906 with old-fashioned elevators/lifts.

voyage.name: Casa França Brasil
voyage.content: French cultural centre built in 1820, with gallery and video hall.

voyage.name: City Hall
voyage.alt: Camara Municipal do Rio de Janeiro
voyage.content: Hosts the city council.

voyage.name: Lapa Viaduct
voyage.content: Colonial structure built in 1750 that brought water from springs to downtown.

voyage.name: Municipal Theatre
voyage.content: City Theatre, inspired by the Paris Opéra House.

voyage.name: National Library
voyage.content: The National Library offers guided tours on weekdays, showing visitors its rare collection, various bookstacks and the catalogue system. Registration with identification is required, and tours run for about an hour. They leave at 13:00 for English tours, and 11:00, 13:00 and 15:00 for Portuguese tours.

voyage.name: Passeio Público
voyage.address: Rua Texeira de Freitas at Rua Mestre Valentim
voyage.content: Commissioned in 1779, this was to become the first public park in the Americas. Check out the original Rococo-style gate and the ironwork fountains.

voyage.name: Petrobras Headquarters
voyage.content: The headquarters for the federal gas (petrol) company is an interesting piece of brutalist architecture which somehow resembles a Rubik's Cube with some blocks missing.

voyage.name: Praça da República
voyage.content: Large park; good for a rest. Look for monkeys and capybaras that roam about.

voyage.name: Sambódromo
voyage.address: Rua Marquês de Sapucaí - Praça Onze
voyage.content: Site of the famous Carnaval parades, the Sambódromo is a long street flanked by grandstands and VIP boxes. From the start of the year until Carnaval week, technical rehearsals (Ensaios Técnicos) free to the public are held on Saturday and Sunday evenings, with 2-3 teams performing per session.

voyage.name: Selarón Steps
voyage.content: A stairway covered by colorful tiles and the ever-evolving art work of Chilean artist Jorge Selarón.

voyage.name: Estátua equestre de D. Pedro I
Glória Inlet
voyage.content: A beautiful spot for a stroll along the bank of Guanabara Bay.

voyage.name: Memorial Monument of Opening Ports - Trade
voyage.alt: Monumento Comemorativo da Abertura dos Portos
voyage.address: Rua do Russel/Praça Luiz de Camões, Glória

voyage.name: Valongo Wharf Archaeological Site
voyage.content: The place where, during the first decades of the 19th century, ships carrying a total of almost a million African slaves landed. When slave trade was banned, freed slaves lived there for some time, eventually the whole area was entirely rebuilt and its dark history was forgotten until 2011, when African amulets and other items of worship were found during construction works. Nowadays the former wharf is an archaeolog

voyage.name: Campo de Santana
voyage.content: It is near the site where Brazil was declared a Republic in 1889. It's also the site of the monument for Republican leader Benjamin Constant.

voyage.name: Gloria Church
voyage.alt: Igreja Nossa Senhora da Glória do Outeiro
voyage.content: Small but interesting church built in 1739. It is more correctly known as the Outeira da Gloria, outeira in Portuguese meaning “knoll” or small hill. The church was well sited to be seen by arriving sailors sailing into Guanabara Bay. The layout consists of two intertwined octagonal prisms. There are some interesting wooden engravings and tiles from Portugal. Best accessed by one of the world’s shortest funiculars fr

voyage.name: Benedictine Monastery of Rio de Janeiro
voyage.content: Colonial architecture. Founded in 1590.

voyage.name: Candelária Church
voyage.alt: Igreja da Nossa Senhora da Candelária
voyage.content: Neoclassic cathedral.

voyage.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of Saint Sebastian
voyage.content: A rather bizarre, modern cathedral shaped like a volcano, with a very impressively vacuous interior.

voyage.name: Our Lady of Mount Carmel Church
voyage.alt: Igreja Nossa Senhora do Carmo da Lapa do Desterro

voyage.name: Church of São Francisco de Paula
voyage.alt: Igreja de São Francisco de Paula, Old Cathedral of Rio de Janeiro
voyage.address: Largo de São Francisco de Paula, 9-11, Centro

voyage.name: Church of Our Lady of Lapa
voyage.alt: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Lapa dos Mercadores

voyage.name: Church of Our Lady of Lampadosa
voyage.alt: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Lampadosa

voyage.name: Church of St. Goncalo and St. George
voyage.alt: São Gonçalo Garcia e São Jorge
voyage.address: Rua Alfandega and Praça da República corner, Centro

voyage.name: St. Francis Church
voyage.address: Largo São Francisco da Prainha, Saúde

voyage.name: Church of St. Francis of Penance
voyage.alt: Convento de Santo Antônio Igreja da Venerável Ordem Terceira de São Francisco da Penitência
voyage.content: Church of the Venerable Third Order of St. Francis of Penance is a part of the Convent of Saint Antony

voyage.name: Churches of Convent Carmo
voyage.alt: Convento Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Carmo da Antiga Sé e Igreja da Ordem Terceira do Carmo
voyage.content: These churches were built in the 18th century as part of a Carmelite Convent. After the future Portuguese King John VI of Portugal arrived in Rio in 1808 the churches became the city’s former main cathedral and the royal chapel. It was the site of coronations, and royal weddings and funerals. it features baroque and rococo architecture, with an ornate gilded interior and intricate wood carvings, mainly by one of Rio'

voyage.name: São Francisco da Penitência Church
voyage.alt: Igreja de São Francisco da Penitência
voyage.content: Colonial church built in 1773.

voyage.name: Monastery of Saint Theresa
voyage.content: Baroque

voyage.name: Church Our Lady of La Salette
voyage.content: Founded in 1914. It has neo Gothic arches. One of the most beautiful church in Rio de Janeiro.

voyage.name: Museum of the Estate of Ceu
voyage.hours: Daily except Tue 12:00-17:00; closed for major holidays
voyage.content: An art and antique museum with a good collection of works by modern masters. During Carnaval 2006 some of its most famous works of art were stolen while a procession passed by outside.

voyage.name: Image and Sound Museum
voyage.alt: Museu da Imagem e do Som
voyage.content: For researchers about the Brazilian film, radio, and broadcasting industries.

voyage.name: Museum of Modern Art
voyage.content: After MASP in São Paulo, the second most important contemporary art museum in Brazil, (downtown, next to Santos Dumont airport). Modernist architecture on the edge of the Bay.

voyage.name: National History Museum
voyage.content: A museum of Brazilian history stretching from colonial to imperial times; big collection of paintings, but poor in artifacts.

voyage.name: Naval and Oceanographic Museum
voyage.content: Installed in a building constructed in 1868, this museum preserves articles from the seafaring history of the city.

voyage.name: National Museum of Fine Arts
voyage.content: Another building modelled on one in Paris, this time the Louvre. Includes large paintings from Academicist and Neoclassical Brazilian artists, as well as many copies of European sculptures

voyage.name: Rio Art Museum
voyage.content: A museum opened in 2013 as part of the regeneration of the old port area. Made up of a new building with good views from the roof, next to a converted building that had been part of Rio’s former bus station. Rotating exhibitions changing annually.

voyage.name: Tram Museum
voyage.content: This small tram museum has photos of and artifacts from the glory days when trams were all over Rio, including some models of old tramcars and lots of electrical equipment.

voyage.name: Museum of Tomorrow
voyage.price: R$30 adults, R$15 youth under 21, free for seniors 60+ or children under 6
voyage.content: Forward-looking science museum in a compact but stunning Santiago Calatrava-designed building.

voyage.name: Military Museum Conde de Linhares
voyage.content: Learn about the history of Brazil's military as you stroll through galleries with exhibits about historic conflicts and leaders. Large collection of military hardware including tanks, field artillery, and rocket launchers.

voyage.name: Gustavo Capanema Palace
voyage.content: Former ministry of culture, designed by French architect Le Corbusier; though small, it is regarded as an important pioneering work in modern architecture.

voyage.name: Ilha Fiscal Palace
voyage.content: The former Customs House for Rio has some fascinating decorations and is well worth the visit.

voyage.name: Itamaraty Palace
voyage.content: Former presidential palace (1889-1893) and foreign office; now hosts a museum of South American diplomacy, a library and the UN information offices in Brazil.

voyage.name: Paço Imperial
voyage.content: Old Imperial Palace built in 1743 (though impressively modest). Colonial architecture.

voyage.name: Tiradentes Palace
voyage.content: The seat of the Legislative Assembly, visitors are welcome to wander in the corridors along the perimeter of the first floor, which tell the history of the Legislative Assembly and the building (mostly in Portuguese). Access to the second floor can be arranged through a guided tour with volunteers at the reception.

voyage.name: Artists' Open House
voyage.content: Held over a few days in May and November of each year, when Santa Teresa's artists open their studios to the public. There are free shuttle buses from most parts of the city for this event.

voyage.name: Mocidade Independente Samba School
voyage.address: Rua Júlio do Carmo, 251 - Cidade Nova

voyage.name: Samba City
voyage.content: This arts and entertainment complex celebrates Carnaval year-round. Thursday nights at 20:00, there is a special Carnaval samba presentation called Forces of Nature (Forças da Natureza), which includes a dinner buffet, for R$190 per person, with students and senior citizens getting half-price.

voyage.name: Santa Teresa Historic Tramway
voyage.content: What was Brazil's only remaining metropolitan tramway, in continuous operation since 1859, ran from Largo da Carioca, across the Arcos da Lapa, and into Santa Teresa terminating at the Largo de Curvelo. The tramway was closed in 2014 after accidents, but as of October 2015 is running again. If you follow the road further up from the last stop, and take the second road to the left, after another 300 m you will reach a

voyage.name: UFRJ School of Music
voyage.alt: Escola de Música da Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro
voyage.content: A good place to catch free classical music concerts. Stop by during the day for a schedule or check the newspaper for events, as the surrounding neighborhood can be a bit shady at night.

voyage.name: Saara
voyage.address: surrounding Rua Buenos Aires between Praça da República and Rua dos Andrades ~Rua da Alfândega, 187
voyage.content: Nothing to do with the desert, this bazaar is named after an association of small shop owners that was established there on the early 1900s, most of them from the Middle East and Jews from Eastern Europe. There are also lots of Chinese businesses. Today, it has a wide variety of shops, selling almost anything. From trousers to gum, from licorice to Carnaval costumes, you can find virtually everything on the always cr

voyage.name: Music shops
voyage.content: While a handcrafted guitar will easily go for thousands of reais, you may want to pick up an inexpensive cavaquinho or cuica. One block north on Rua 7 de Setembro there are some CD and record shops, though their offerings are meager.

voyage.name: Bistrô do Paço
voyage.content: Quick and quiet spot for a light lunch.

voyage.name: Al-Kuwait
voyage.content: A good place to try the Brazilian take on Middle Eastern food.

voyage.name: Cafe Colombo
voyage.content: Dates back to 1894 and has a dazzling tea room and arguably the best sweets and other delicacies in town.

voyage.name: Pizzaria Guanabara
voyage.content: Delivery service. - Other units: Avenida Ataulfo de Paiva, 1228 - Leblon. (+55 21 2294-0797), - Avenida Armando Lombardi, 75, Loja A - Barra da Tijuca, (+55 21 3153-4040).

voyage.name: Olla Gourmet
voyage.content: Buffet and cafe of salads, different meats, and desserts.

voyage.name: Restaurante Nova Capela
voyage.content: Try the house specialty of mutton with rice and broccoli (carneiro com arroz com brócolis).

voyage.name: Pilão de Pedra Restaurant
voyage.content: Another weigh & pay buffet that includes sushi.

voyage.name: Restaurant Sobrenatural
voyage.content: Has some of the freshest fish in Rio. Go on Monday, Wednesday or Friday, when they have live samba and chorinho music by renowned artists. Try their moqueca dishes. Air Conditioning.

voyage.name: Ponto de Encontro Ximeninho
voyage.content: Come here for some comfort Brazilian food, little fritters and feijoada and a Brahma to wash it down.

voyage.name: Aprazível
voyage.content: This restaurante mineiro, inside an antique villa, has nice veranda and garden seating with great views of Guanabara Bay. Reservations recommended.

voyage.name: Espirito Santa
voyage.content: Another fine restaurant in an old villa built in the 1930s, this eatery serves exotic dishes from the Amazon region, including fish such as piranha, and unusual fruits like cupuaçu, taperabá, and jambu. They also have a good selection of regional cachaças.

voyage.name: Armazém São Thiago (Bar do Gomez)
voyage.content: A beautifully restored former grocery store, with a high ceiling, nice wooden furnishings, and beer that's always ice-cold. Located a bit past where most tourists get off the tram, and frequented by an eclectic local crowd which spills out on to the sidewalk even in the afternoon.

voyage.name: Bar Simplesmente
voyage.address: Rua Pascoal Carlos Magno, 115 - Santa Teresa
voyage.content: Lively and popular with the young crowd. And not simply a bar; the food is inexpensive but good.

voyage.name: Beco do Rato
voyage.content: This is in fact not a club but a street party. This place was a quite small and hidden beer and beverage deposit store. After a change in the administration it changed into a bar, offering good quality live music, and turned into one of the nicest street parties in Rio. Laid-back atmosphere typical of Rio, samba and beer. Is surrounded by historical buildings in this old forgotten spot of Lapa. On Tuesdays they have

voyage.name: Goya Beira
voyage.content: Pleasant little place for a drink or two, with a view of Praça Neves with the tram line. If you get hungry, try the pizza.

voyage.name: Carioca da Gema
voyage.content: Located in a nice old house from the 1900s, this place always has good samba groups playing. One of the best days is on Monday nights when on stage you can see one of the most powerful voices of samba, the singer Richah, with his group playing old Carnaval songs.

voyage.name: Circo Voador
voyage.content: Live music venue with plenty of live Carioca music.

voyage.name: Clube Dos Democraticos
voyage.content: Clube dos Democráticos was founded in 1867 and is one of the first carnaval groups of Rio. Nowadays the great ballroom of the beginning of the 20th century houses one of the best places to dance Brazilian rhythms, especially samba, in Rio. Best days are Wednesday and Thursday. Wednesday is the day of Forró (a Brazilian rhythm from Northeast really popular throughout the country) and on Thursday the traditional samba.

voyage.name: Rio Scenarium
voyage.content: One of the most beautiful and best-known samba clubs in Rio de Janeiro. Was once elected by the British newspaper The Guardian as being one of the top 10 bars in the world. Nice decor, filled with antiques, paintings, medieval armors, old bicycles, etc., in an amazing 19th-century warehouse. Three floors: on the first floor the main stage, second floor is an annex where sometimes another band plays or there is a DJ p

voyage.name: Sacadura 154
voyage.content: Dance club.

voyage.name: Pousada Favelinha
voyage.address: Rua Almirante Alexandrino 2023 - between Laranjeiras and Santa Teresa
voyage.content: Might be your choice if staying in a favela is your cup of tea.

voyage.name: Casa MangoMango
voyage.price: From US$80, R$330-750 (US$130-280) per night in Carneval season
voyage.content: A bed & breakfast that offers nice prices for couples and groups. Great view, too!.

voyage.name: ibis Rio de Janeiro Centro
voyage.content: Three-star hotel. Rooms: 250.

voyage.name: Hotel Inglês
voyage.content: Nice location next to the park, but a bit overpriced compared to similar accommodation in the area.

voyage.name: Casa Beleza
voyage.price: Doubles from US$90, loft suite R$330, orange room R$280, blue room R$240 (2014)
voyage.content: Charming guest house in an exotic mansion with swimming pool and tropical gardens. The house was the former residence of the Governor of the State of Rio.

voyage.name: Maracanã Stadium
voyage.address: Av. Presidente Castelo Branco at Av. Maracanã
voyage.content: Once the world's highest capacity football venue, it was able to hold nearly 200,000 people. In modern times, the capacity has been reduced because of safety considerations, and the introduction of seating for all fans. It is undergoing renovation, to expand it to hold 80,000. The matches of Rio's football clubs like Flamengo or Fluminense are usually far from full, so go along and watch a game. There is also a Socce

voyage.name: Tijuca National Park
voyage.alt: Parque Nacional da Tijuca, Sector Florestal
voyage.address: Estrada da Cascatinha, 850 - Alto da Boa Vista
voyage.content: A few km north of the beach, this mountainous subtropical forest is Brazil's smallest national park. It is largely hand-planted as much of the original forest was destroyed to make way for coffee plantations. Despite this it contains hundreds of species, many of which are threatened with extinction. Corcovado is to the east of the park but if you really want to appreciate what the park has to offer you have to drive

voyage.name: Engenhão Stadium
voyage.address: Rua Arquias Cordeiro - Engenho de Dentro
voyage.content: Estádio Olímpico João Havelange, known by its nickname of Engenhão, is a new soccer stadium built for the Pan-American Games of 2007. A modern construction, not as big as Maracanã but still worth a visit for soccer fans. The Botafogo team plays its matches there.

voyage.name: Grajaú State Park
voyage.content: This 55-hectare park preserves some of the original forest and serves as a refuge for a wide range of species including marmosets, bush dogs, guinea pigs, parakeets, vultures, and hawks. The park includes the Pedra do Andaraí, symbol of the area.

voyage.name: Museum of Astronomy and Related Sciences
voyage.alt: Museu de Astronomia e Ciências Afins (MAST)
voyage.content: Also has an observatory.

voyage.name: Museum of the First Reign
voyage.content: A museum about the reign of Emperor Pedro I (1822-1831), but with a modest collection.

voyage.name: Musical sidewalks of Vila Isabel
voyage.content: The mosaic sidewalks along Boulevard 28 de Setembro between Praça Maracanã and Praça Barão de Drummond are musical staves. Written in the stones are 20 complete musical works, including tunes by Ary Barroso, Martinho da Vila, Almirante, Noel Rosa, and other famous Brazilian composers who frequented Vila Isabel back in its Bohemian heyday. If you know who these guys are, you might also be interested in checking out th

voyage.name: Rio de Janeiro Zoo
voyage.address: Parque Quinta da Boa Vista - São Cristóvão
voyage.content: If you won't be making it to the Amazon or the Pantanal, this is a good place to see some of Brazil's more exotic creatures.

voyage.name: Train Museum
voyage.address: Rua Arquias Cordeiro 1046 - Engenho de Dentro
voyage.content: A modest collection of 19th-century engines, train cars used by emperors and presidents, and streetcars.

voyage.name: Museu do Açude
voyage.address: Estrada do Açude, 764 - Alto da Boa Vista
voyage.content: The former residence of one of the founders of the Modern Art Museum, this museum hosts a collection of items from the history of Portuguese rule, including furniture, kitchenware, and an array of azulejos, or Portuguese blue tiles. There are also separate collections of Oriental art and Brazilian pop art.

voyage.name: Quinta da Boa Vista
voyage.content: Park

voyage.name: Church of Our Lady of Lourdes
Chapel of St. Roque
voyage.address: Rua Padre Juvenal, s/n - Praça de São Roque - Ilha de Paquetá

voyage.name: Church of the Good Lord Jesus of the Hill
voyage.alt: Igreja Matriz do Senhor Bom Jesus do Monte
voyage.address: Praia dos Tamoios, 45 - Ilha de Paquetá

voyage.name: Convent of Our Lady of Help
voyage.alt: Convento de Nossa Senhora da Ajuda
voyage.address: Praça Barão de Drumond, Vila Isabel

voyage.name: Rock climbing
voyage.content: Many climbers take on the 444-meter Pedra do Andaraí, in Grajaú State Park. See the See section for details.

voyage.name: Ramos
voyage.content: A popular, in-bay, beach where the government built an artificial pool on the sand (piscinão). This area is not recommended for foreigners to visit. Inappropriate for bathing.

voyage.name: Unidos de Vila Isabel
voyage.content: Founded in 1948, the city's fastest-growing samba school is now the third largest.

voyage.name: Unidos da Tijuca
voyage.content: Conceived in 1931.

voyage.name: Norte Shopping
voyage.content: The largest shopping mall in the Zona Norte, with two food courts, cinemas, and a range of stores and restaurants. Fitness center BodyTech (the largest fitness club in Brazil); Striker Bowling, Kinoplex UCI cinema (with 10 rooms, 3D), Magic Games playhouse, Mega bookstore. Cafes:Kopenhagen, Mc Cafe, Viena Café; Chocolate shops: Brasil Cacau, Cacau Show, Chocomundi. Pubs.

voyage.name: Feira Nordestina
voyage.address: Associacao Do Feirante da Feira de São Cristóvão
voyage.content: A great place to shop with plenty of stalls selling all sorts of food, textiles and local goods. Also a good place to get a taste of Brazilian culture from the northeast. Food, dance and music tantalize all the senses.

voyage.name: Madureira Market
voyage.content: A popular market where there are cheap bars and restaurants, plus little shops selling everything you can imagine, including everything you need for Afro-Brazilian rituals (statues, candles, food and animals). Not usually visited by gringos, but still an interesting place if you want to see how normal people live and have fun outside the Zona Sul.

voyage.name: Nova América Outlet Shopping
voyage.address: Avenida Pastor Martin Luther King Júnior 126 - Inhaúma
voyage.content: One of the cheaper malls in the city.

voyage.name: Shopping Boulevard
voyage.address: Rua Barão de São Francisco 236 - Vila Isabel
voyage.content: Large shopping mall with 210 stores, a food court and a Kinoplex cinema.

voyage.name: Adega Carne-de-Sol do Peixto
voyage.content: As the name suggests they are best at carne-de-sol. They have a full menu of typical Brazilian food in good-sized helpings.

voyage.name: Adegão Português
voyage.content: This hole-in-the-wall joint has fantastic food that has attracted fans for over four decades. Lamb with vegetables and potatoes is a must-try.

voyage.name: Fiorino Bar e Restaurante
voyage.content: Good-quality Italian restaurant with reasonable prices. Note that they do not accept credit cards.

voyage.name: Petisco da Vila
voyage.content: This restaurant has for decades been the haunt of famous bohemian composers and poets such as Noel Rosa and Martinho da Vila. It remains the hotspot of Vila Isabel, with daily buffets, and feijoada on Saturdays. It also holds the distinction of having the highest annual draft beer sales of any restaurant in Brazil. Accepts Visa.

voyage.name: Restaurante Quinta da Boa Vista
voyage.content: Fine dining in what used to be the chapel for the Imperial Palace. The food is a fantastic display of traditional Brazilian cuisine with formal service.

voyage.name: Restaurante Salete
voyage.content: Famous for its shrimp risotto and empadinhas. Delivery available. Accepts credit cards.

voyage.name: Pa Pa G
voyage.content: Gay and lesbian nightclub.

voyage.name: Barraco #55
voyage.address: Rua da Assembleia #19, Nova Brasilia, Complexo do Alemão
voyage.content: An arts and research centre and hostel at the same time in the middle of the favela Complexo do Alemão. Run by the friendly and helpful Dutch Ellen and her Brazilian partner, who will include you in the local life and culture festivals. Very authentic and enjoyable place to stay, different from the usual tourist life in Rio.

voyage.name: Rio Aeroporto Hotel
voyage.address: inside Galeão International Airport, 3rd floor, Sector B
voyage.content: A good place to stay if you arrive late to Rio or are leaving early in the morning. Clean rooms with all the convenience of being within the airport. Rooms have no windows.

voyage.name: Linx Hotel International Airport Galeão
voyage.address: Located in: RIOgaleão - Tom Jobim International Airport
voyage.content: Only has 15 rooms for those who are stuck in the airport. Rooms have TV, telephone and air conditioning but no windows.

voyage.name: Aerospace Museum
voyage.content: Good collection of planes, engines, etc. and a chance to see how Air Traffic Control works.

voyage.name: Barra Woods
voyage.address: Av. das Americas, km.6 - Barra da Tijuca
voyage.content: This 560,000-m² park is one of the most visited green areas in the Zona Oeste, with a lake, walking trails through the woods, large lawns, playgrounds, and sporting facilities.

voyage.name: Casa do Pontal Popular Art Museum
voyage.address: Estrada do Pontal 3295 - Recreio dos Bandeirantes
voyage.content: The area's most important collection of popular arts and crafts.

voyage.name: Chico Mendes Ecological Park
voyage.address: Avenida Jarbas de Carvalho 679 - Recreio dos Bandeirantes
voyage.content: This 43-hectare park has walking trails through a preserved section of the Mata Atlântica (Atlantic Forest). They also offer a guided tour of the habitats of several local endangered species, including the three-toed sloth, the broad-snouted caiman, and the red-footed tortoise. There is an exhibit hall with exhibits on local wildlife.

voyage.name: Pedra Branca State Park
voyage.content: The largest ecological park in the city, and the largest urban forest in the world, with 12,500 hectares. Vegetation is typical of the old Atlantic forest, and fauna includes ocelots, sloths, armadillos, and toucans. Beyond the nature, there are also ruins of several structures, such as old farmhouses.

voyage.name: Church of Our Lady of Loreto
voyage.alt: Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Loreto
voyage.content: WEeest

voyage.name: Church of Our Lady of the Conception
voyage.content: A modern church

voyage.name: Cidade das Artes
voyage.content: Large complex with cultural events at the heart of Barra.

voyage.name: Sítio Roberto Burle Marx
voyage.content: The garden of landscape architect and artist Roberto Burle Marx (1909-1994), with a collection of plants from all over Brazil. In 2021 it was listed as a world heritage site.

voyage.name: Abricó beach
voyage.content: Nudist beach. Facilities and telephone service are quite limited, so plan ahead.

voyage.name: Pedra do Telégrafo
voyage.content: Hike up this 354-m-high mountain and enjoy a beautiful view. Famous for the "cliffhanger images", which can be taken on top.

voyage.name: Rio Water Planet
voyage.content: A water park with over 40 attractions, located in Vargem Grande.

voyage.name: Barra Shopping
voyage.address: Avenida das Américas 4666 - Barra da Tijuca
voyage.content: The largest mall in South America, and one of the most popular malls in the city. Leather goods are some of the best bargains here. Shoes and belts are especially inexpensive. Kopenhagen chocolate shop has some of the best chocolates. It is quite nice to stop and have a coffee at one of the several coffee shops and people watch. Many of the guards are rather attractive ladies, but are quite serious about their job. S

voyage.name: Downtown Barra da Tijuca
voyage.content: An urban development intended to match the density and mixed-use nature of a traditional downtown area. There are many shops, botiques, cafes, restaurants, offices, and a movie theater complex. A small park can be found nestled in a quiet corner of the complex. At night, the shops close and the nightlife begins. Live music can be found at any of several restaurants. When the music is particularly good, the area aroun

voyage.name: New York City Center
voyage.address: Avenida das Américas 5000 - Barra da Tijuca

voyage.name: Rio Design Barra
voyage.address: Avenida das Américas 7777 - Barra da Tijuca
voyage.content: The poshest mall in the area. Top Brazilian designers have opened stores there, making it an option for the affluent population in Barra who does not want to drive to São Conrado Fashion Mall. The mall also has excellent restaurant options and two movie theaters. Much less crowded and a lot more charming than most shopping centers in Rio. Worth the visit.

voyage.name: Cabana do Pepe
voyage.content: Pepe was a famous hang glider who passed away in a hang gliding accident in Japan a few years ago. He started a sandwich shop on the beach that makes a variety of healthy sandwiches. Especially good are the fruit smoothies. Not to be missed. Cabana do Pepe is run by Pepe's widow. This is the most popular area of the Barra beach, and is the best area for people watching.

voyage.name: Alpendre
voyage.content: Alpendre's menu is full of typical Brazilian cuisine from around the country.

voyage.name: Beco do Alemão
voyage.address: Avenida das Americas 1600 - Barra da Tijuca
voyage.content: Although unexpected it is delightful. Germany food in Rio! Fantastic breakfast and salad bar.

voyage.name: Caminho do Mar
voyage.content: Excellent vegan option with three-course meals in a more lush quarter of Recreio. Offers pizza delivery on Saturdays. Prices can be a bit steep for locals.

voyage.name: Rio/Brasa
voyage.address: Avenida Ayrton Senna 2541 - Barra da Tijuca
voyage.content: This churrascaria has unusually excellent meat and shrimp along with a salad bar and all the other standards of the genre. There is a monitored play area for children.

voyage.name: Bar do Baiano
voyage.content: Bar with a varied schedule of live music from Monday to Saturday, covering all types of music, from jazz to choro.
